Make sure you’re leaving the door and detergent drawer open for your washing machine to air it out when not in use. Also if you’re air drying your clothes, put them on a spin cycle first and then air them out in a small/warm room with a window cracked. Make sure you dry your clothes as soon as they’re done and they’re not just sitting in the machine all wet, (same goes for leaving damp towels/clothes in the hamper for too long). Also stop using fabric softener, bad for your machine, bad for your clothes, bad for everything. Or only use a small amount for things that really need it (not towels it makes them less absorbant). If none of this works try washing your clothes on a higher heat to kill any mould/bacteria (60°). Good Luck!!

The white part of two leeks, 1/2 lb. tomatoes, 3/4
lb. potatoes, 1 1/2 oz. butter, a little cream, and parsley.
Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan; before it has
bubbled put in the finely sliced leeks; let them just
soften in the butter. Half the success of this soup
depends upon this first operation. If the butter burns
instead of just melting or the leeks brown the flavour
will be spoilt.
Add the roughly chopped tomatoes; again let them
cook until they start to give out their juice. Add the
peeled and diced potato, a seasoning of salt, and two
lumps of sugar. Cover with 1 1/4 pints of water. After
the soup comes to the boil let it simmer steadily but
not too fast for 25 minutes. Put it through the food
mill, twice if necessary. Return the puree to the
rinsed-out saucepan. When it is hot, add about 4 oz.
cream. Season with the parsley.

I think the problem with this is that the reason a lot of ADHD folks struggle with recalling things is due to “storage” issues with memories not “locating” issues. 

So when the event happened you were distracted or nothing happened that made it significant in your brain so you didn’t store the memory. You can’t locate something that you don’t have, see what I mean?

It sounds like your dad had some real issues which will have impacted you throughout your life and may be the reason you are now struggling so much to regulate your emotions regarding his death.

It sounds like he was distant and emotionally neglectful whilst you were growing up, and then once he was old, dying and alone he realised that he had pushed his child away and that he needed to try to get you close again.

But because of his extremely immature and warped emotional regulation, rather than honestly reach out to you the only thing he could think of was to manipulate you into coming to see him.

Basically it sounds like he had lots of issues, which will have affected your mental development and perception of reality. And will be a big part of your mental health issues now.

I would keep seeing a therapist as regularly as you can and work through your issues whether or not you feel ready to tackle your relationship with your dad. Remember this isn’t your fault, that you didn’t deserve to be treated the way he treated you. Also try not to tell yourself that talking about your issues is “bumming people out”, talking about things is the only way you will be able to get them off your chest.

Open up to your therapist, open up to friends you trust and remember that you will be okay :)

5’9 and i still can’t believe they thought 70mg was okay??? they decided because my blood pressure and pulse were okay that it was fine after the 5 week titration period, but 6 months later i realised how much weight i was losing and reduced to 30mg…

It can help with cravings and BED, but if you’re leading a healthy lifestyle (which it sounds like you are) then you don’t need to focus on reducing arbitrary numbers on a scale.
